# hands/x402

Teeny's x402 rail: keep it funded, and pay for web search with it.

## How to call it

Run it from the repository root with your shell (exec) tool: `hands/x402 <verb> [flags]`.

- A verb that takes a body reads one JSON object from stdin. Everything else is flags.
- It prints one JSON object on stdout. Exit 0 is success. Exit 2 is a refusal by a rule, the guard or a cap: read the `rule` and `reason`, and do not retry it unchanged. Any other exit is an error.
- Secrets belong to the hand; you never see them and never pass one.
- The hand runs the guard, its caps and `DRY_RUN` itself. `DRY_RUN` is on unless the box turned it off; under it an acting verb checks every rule and sends nothing. Do not try to go around the hand, and do not look for another way to do what it refused.

## Side effects

- Acting (side effects in the world, each goes through the guard and the caps): search QUERY [--n N] [--type auto|fast|deep] [--contents text|highlights|summary]; contents URL...; crawl QUERY [--n N] [--scrape]
- Job (writes state or calls the core): fund
- Operator only (never call): none
- Read only: fund status; log [--max N]

## Verbs

| Verb | Kind | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `fund` | J | Tops up USDC on Base when it is under the floor, through `wallet` `swap`/`bridge` (below). |
| `fund status` | R | The floor, the target and the daily cap, USDC on Base now (one `eth_call`), what was topped up in the last 24 hours, the last five runs. |
| `log [--max N]` | R | The wallet's paid requests (`x402_requests`, as `wallet x402 log`) and the top-up runs (`x402_fund_runs`), newest first. |
| `search QUERY [--n N] [--type auto\|fast\|deep] [--contents text\|highlights\|summary]` | A | Exa web search, paid over x402 (below). |
| `contents URL...` | A | Exa's text of 1..10 http(s) pages, paid over x402. |
| `crawl QUERY [--n N] [--scrape]` | A | Firecrawl's x402 search. |

Kinds: R = read: no side effect beyond its read cache; A = acting: posts, sends, pays or opens something in the world; O = operator-only: the operator runs it, never you; J = job: writes state or calls the core, says nothing to anyone; scheduled jobs run it, you do not.

Verbs named in the hand's source: `contents`, `crawl`, `fund`, `log`, `search`.

Flags named in the hand's source: `--contents`, `--max`, `--n`, `--scrape`, `--type`.

For one verb's exact flags, run `DRY_RUN=1 hands/x402 <verb> --help`. The full account is in docs/hands.md.
